title: CHAPTER 9: TRIBES, SOCIAL STRUCTURE AND MOVEMENTS

blocks.content: Andhra Pradesh is home to a significant tribal population, particularly in the hilly and forested regions of the state. The tribal (Girijan) belts are concentrated in the Agency areas of northern Andhra (Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram, Srikakulam) and parts of East Godavari.

cells: Srikakulam, Vizianagaram; known for wall paintings called 'Idital'
East Godavari, West Godavari along Godavari River; Koya rebellion (1922)
Throughout AP; nomadic traders historically; colorful costume; own dialect – Gor Boli
Spread across AP; traditionally forest-dwelling; ancestor worship
Nallamala Hills (Kurnool, Prakasam, Nalgonda border); considered most primitive; Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG); associated with Nagarjunasagar area
Throughout AP; fortune tellers and basket weavers
Nellore, Chittoor; coastal and forest dwellers; PVTG
Jagannatha Raju and Sitarama Raju led revolt against British over taxation
Led by Alluri Sitarama Raju in East Godavari / Visakhapatnam tribal areas; against British oppression of tribals and disarming of tribal population; Alluri was captured and shot in 1924
Multiple uprisings of Koya tribe against forest restrictions and exploitation
Post-independence; AP has seen multiple movements related to prohibition; women's anti-arrack movement 1992 (Nellore district) led to state-wide prohibition
Demand for separate Telugu state; Potti Sriramulu's fast unto death on 15 December 1952 led to creation of Andhra State on 1 October 1953
Demand for separate Telangana state; eventually led to bifurcation in June 2014
Women's uprising in Dubagunta village, Nellore; women forced closure of liquor shops; spread statewide; resulted in historic prohibition policy
Controversy over location of AP's new capital; three-capital proposal (Amaravati, Kurnool, Visakhapatnam) generated protests
Demand for a steel plant in Visakhapatnam; eventually led to establishment of RINL/Vizag Steel
